title: All the key moments from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix
excerpt:
Lando Norris claimed victory in a wet thriller at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, while Mercedes did enough to secure the 2026 Constructors' Championship.

There were plenty of story lines up and down the grid, including a runner-up finish for Max Verstappen after starting at the back of the grid, while the wet weather gave midfield runner Liam Lawson the chance to shine.

Here are all the key moments from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix…

Norris overcomes the weather to make it back-to-back Sao Paulo wins

Interlagos proved to be a happy hunting ground for Norris last season, the McLaren driver taking victory 12 months ago en route to the title at the end of the season.

Having taken back-to-back wins in the summer this term, Norris and McLaren had failed to feature in the lead battle of recent Grands Prix due to a lack of outright pace, but the combination looked strong in Brazil's dry practice running.

That pace translated over to the wet as well, with Norris claiming pole during Saturday's thunderstorms as he looked like a genuine contender for victory no matter the elements.

The Briton's task became harder, though, as he immediately lost his advantage to fellow front row starter Kimi Antonelli off the line, and lost a further spot through the opening corners to Lawson.

Recovering P2 as Lawson's intermediate tyres overheated, Norris pitted a lap earlier than Antonelli for slick rubber, slashing a 7s gap in the process and, shortly after, forcing the Mercedes driver into a spin at Turn 1.

Thereafter, Norris controlled the pace at the front of the field, managing tricky conditions in the final stages after switching to intermediate tyres and claiming his third win of the season by 14s from Verstappen.

“The main thing today was I just kept it cool and I didn't make any mistakes," said Norris. "I had the pace when I needed to, so it was good. Nice to be back on the top step, and what a place to do it as well.”

Norris delighted to ‘give something back’ to McLaren with Sao Paulo win

Mercedes clinch constructors’ title despite spins for Russell and Antonelli

Mercedes entered the weekend all but assured of claiming a constructors' title for the first time since 2021, just one weekend after Antonelli claimed his maiden drivers' crown.

The Italian was outpaced, however, by team mate George Russell in the wet Qualifying session, as the pair finished second and third quickest.

Russell had been left annoyed after missing out on pole when backing out of his lap in the best of the conditions, but the Briton had to serve a five-place grid penalty for an Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) change, dropping him to P7 on the grid.

There was drama even before the start for Antonelli, with the new World Champion running wide at Turn 12 on his reconnaissance lap and spinning his car on the grass, before scrambling back to the pits undamaged.

As Antonelli grabbed the lead at the start, Russell worked his way up the order and pitted from P4 as drivers moved to slick tyres, only for him to spin on the damp pit exit.

After recovering to point the right way, Russell continued on the fringes of the top 10, while Antonelli lost his lead to Norris after a spin of his own at Turn 1.

Antonelli would lose further places after running wide at the opening corner to the Red Bull duo, while rain in the closing stages meant a stop for intermediate tyres, with Russell allowed to pass his team mate for P4.

Antonelli finished P5 and remained there despite being handed a five-second penalty post-race for an unsafe pit release at his final stop, the result not denying Mercedes this year's title.

Verstappen completes another epic Sao Paulo recovery

It was yet another epic recovery drive from Verstappen in Sao Paulo as the Red Bull driver stormed to the podium from the back of the grid.

He had taken a penalty after having several power unit components changed on his car but sliced through the field in the opening laps, eventually finishing in P2.

Interlagos has proved to be a happy hunting ground for Verstappen in recent seasons, winning the 2024 Grand Prix in the wet from P17, and finishing third last year after starting in the pit lane.

It was a double podium for Red Bull too, with Isack Hadjar finishing in P3 – the second double of the season after the duo did the same in Baku.

Having started in P4, the Frenchman moved up to P2 during the middle section of the race but received team orders to let Verstappen by after running wide and losing time at Turn 1.

Verstappen reflects on 'challenging' Sao Paulo GP as he charges from P21 to the podium

Ferrari's 'complete disaster'

Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton only scored six points between them, marking a disappointing race for Ferrari.

Hamilton had an impressive opening lap on his 400th F1 start, with an incredible charge through the field gaining him 11 places from his P20 grid position following his power unit grid penalties.

However, the performance of his intermediate tyres rapidly declined and he dropped back, hindered further by an investigation into him leaving the track and gaining an advantage, and a late spin – which all contributed to his P9 finish.

Meanwhile, Leclerc also had a grid drop penalty after replacing his ICE, but could not follow his team mate up the order in the opening laps.

He did gradually gain positions through the pit stops and switched to intermediate tyres at the right time, allowing him to cling on as the rain started to fall and eventually fight his way past Lawson for P7.

However, he was given a post-race five-second penalty for contact with the New Zealander, dropping him to P8 – with the Monegasque calling the day a “complete disaster”.

Lawson impresses yet again from the midfield

Lawson has been quietly putting together a very strong season for Racing Bulls, the Kiwi racer lying ninth in the standings, a long way clear of Pierre Gasly in P10.

His more than decent form was evident in Brazil, where he qualified fifth in Saturday’s rainstorm, showing he has what it takes in the wet before mixing it with the front runners from his P3 starting slot on Sunday, courtesy of grid penalties.

He overtook Norris on the opening lap as he got his elbows out, and even chased after Antonelli, before dropping back once the faster cars began to recover.

Nonetheless, he finished best of the midfield, showed his defensive skills in battling Leclerc late on to beat both Ferraris on a day where mistakes were easy to make. That scored his team more valuable points as they look to seal P5 in the teams’ standings.

Despite all of that, and despite having more than double the amount of points as his team mate Arvid Lindblad, Lawson is still not assured of his seat on the grid next year. Racing Bulls have yet to announce either driver for 2027, with Nikola Tsolov the man waiting in the wings.

Lawson has scored in 15 of the 20 Grands Prix contested so far this season, with a top finish of fifth back in Monaco. He even adapted well in his stint at Red Bull, jumping back up to the team in place of the injured Hadjar for three rounds, but whether all that is enough to secure a drive next season remains to be seen.

A contract extension for Interlagos as Brazil delivers another outstanding race

The Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace, better known as Interlagos, will be on the F1 calendar until at least 2035, something the drivers and fans have both rejoiced at.

That contract extension was announced ahead of a thrilling wet Qualifying session that saw the drivers show all their skills and no small amount of bravery as they barrelled around in treacherous conditions.

The Grand Prix delivered on action as well, with Verstappen once again carving his name into the record books with another superb recovery drive from the back all the way to P2. Hamilton also cut his way through early on, while there were spins, strategy dilemmas and plenty of overtakes to enjoy.

The track simply does not deliver straightforward Grands Prix, and with so many titles having been decided here down the years, it has seen the full range of emotions from some of the greats of the sport.

And with Ayrton Senna’s face easy to spot from some of the art around the paddock, Interlagos always offers a touch of nostalgia along with some brilliant racing.

title: How Lawson stated his case with a brilliant Brazilian weekend
excerpt:
For Liam Lawson the Sao Paulo Grand Prix weekend could hardly have gone any better, and the sight of a Racing Bulls car overtaking Lando Norris on the first lap to run in second place was something that nobody could have predicted.

While he would no doubt have liked to have finished higher up the order than the P7 that he ultimately earned, realistically it was never going to be easy to keep the cars from the four top teams behind him – even in a race impacted at both the start and finish by a damp track.

It was a superb P5 in Saturday’s Qualifying that set up Lawson’s strong race. Penalties for others promoted him to third on the grid, and from there a good start and a poor launch by Norris allowed him to get into second, behind only Kimi Antonelli.

However, his intermediates were soon past their best, and he dropped back behind Norris, Isack Hadjar, George Russell and Max Verstappen.

“I mean, crazy race,” he said. “Honestly, I had a really good start. Good grip in Turn 1. Obviously made up a place, and then to be honest, I was thinking I might try and attack Kimi at some point in the lap.

“But yeah, just once the pace stabilises, they're a lot quicker than us, and we started to pull back. We were damaging our tyre, I think, quite a lot more than them. And then I think the pace on the dry was okay.”

Lawson wasn’t the only driver to struggle as their intermediates got older in that opening stint, with Lewis Hamilton also falling away after his good opening run.

“I think it's a bit of graining,” said Lawson. “The problem is that you never know whether to push through the graining and try and wear it all off, or to try and look after the tyre and stop the graining."

“And when it's dry like this, you can't really do much. So for us, the graining started halfway through Lap 1, honestly. And I think for us, we were never really going to be able to keep those cars there anyway. So I'll go and review it, and see if there's something else I could have done.”

As the race progressed on slick tyres Lawson lost places to Oscar Piastri and a recovering Russell. When the rain returned in the closing laps he still had high hopes of hanging onto P7 on the road, but he lost out to a resurgent Charles Leclerc – who gave him a friendly nudge along the way.

“Then at the end, I tried to keep Charles there,” said Lawson. “We had some contact in [Turn] 12. I'll go and review it. I don't really know exactly what to say yet, but obviously I ended up losing the place.”

He also initially feared that he might pick up a puncture: “I think it was his wing that hit my tyre, so I think we got really lucky. I feel like it was exactly like his GP2 move in Abu Dhabi, on Albon years ago. He did the same kind of thing, so maybe it's his specialty. I don't know if it's legal or not! We'll obviously go and review it, but it was a good battle overall.”

The stewards duly decided it wasn’t legal, and gave Leclerc a penalty that promoted Lawson from his P8 at the flag back to P7.

“I feel like we maximised today,” Lawson continued. “I had a had a strong race. I would have liked it to stay wet the whole race. It would have been cool. I probably would have had more of a shot there. But at the moment, we're topping the midfield as a team, and that's what we're targeting every weekend.”

Indeed the points he earned have extended the healthy advantage Racing Bulls already had over Alpine in the battle for P5. However, he’s taking nothing for granted, despite the big gap.

“We've seen it before,” he said. “We had it here a few years ago with Alpine, so we're not going to settle until it's done. But we're in a great place. The car is very, very strong. A couple more races to go, so I'm excited to finish off the season.”

Regarding the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the next round on the calendar, he added: “I think there we're expecting Alpine to be quite strong. They're very, very quick down the straights. So I imagine they'll be strong there. So yeah, let's see.”

Meanwhile, like everyone else, Lawson is awaiting firm news on the 2027 Racing Bulls line-up, with Nikola Tsolov waiting in the wings, and a decision promised soon by team boss Alan Permane.

“I appreciate all the support I'e seen over the last few weeks,” he said. “It's honestly really nice to see. Obviously, I would love it if it was more from a team! But at the moment, I'm just trying to enjoy driving the car because with everything else going on, I don't really know what else I'm meant to do.

“I don't know what else I'm meant to say to you guys. I'm just going to keep driving and yeah, see what happens. I feel like Alan's been extremely supportive to me, and I appreciate that a lot, and I have enjoyed working closely with them and with the team this year. But obviously it's a big organisation.”

title: Antonelli ‘grateful’ for team glory amid Brazil frustration
excerpt:
Although Kimi Antonelli felt “extremely disappointed” by his P5 finish at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, he was more than willing to shed those emotions in favour of celebrating Mercedes’ victory in the Constructors’ Championship.

Having clinched his own title a week ago in Mexico City, Antonelli arrived at Interlagos with a spring in his step, especially after he was confirmed to line up P2 for the race start.

He snatched the lead from polesitter Lando Norris and opened up a confident margin before pitting for slicks slightly later than his rivals, which left him vulnerable when the Briton closed the gap with his up-to-temperature soft tyres.

As Antonelli struggled for grip, he spun off at Turn 1 and watched Norris sail past, then reported that the car felt as though it was “steering by itself”.

Mercedes could find no clear issue, and although he temporarily moved back into first, he didn’t have the pace to stay there and had to settle for fifth behind team mate George Russell – a position he clung onto despite receiving a five-second time penalty for an unsafe release.

While it may not have been the win Antonelli was targeting, the result was still more than enough for the Silver Arrows to clinch their first teams’ title since 2021, prompting a heartfelt post-race celebration on the podium.

“I’m extremely disappointed with the race, but I’m going to put it aside, because today is a great day for the team,” Antonelli reflected. “They all deserve it, an incredible group of people.

“Not only here at the track, but everyone back at the factory – Brackley, Brixworth. They all deserve it, so I’m very happy for them.

“I’m very grateful to be part of this group, because they were the ones to help me to achieve this dream of mine. I’m very happy for them.”

Their achievement also marked the first time Mercedes have won both championships since 2020, which Antonelli hoped would put them on the front foot for the final triple header and fast-approaching 2027 season.

Asked whether he’s excited to have an opportunity to process the last two rounds, he replied: “Yeah, of course. I’m looking forward to it, and looking forward to the end of the season.

“I really want to finish on a high and hopefully come back… finish with a couple more wins, and finish the season on a high. All we want is to keep the momentum going, as well into 2027, and the goal is to keep being successful.”

title: What the teams said – Race day in Brazil
excerpt:
McLaren

Norris sealed his third win of the season and second in a row at Interlagos with a strong drive in tricky conditions. He was overtaken off the line and dropped to third, but once his tyres were up to temperature he started to motor forward. He was lucky to pick up the lead easily when Antonelli spun off, but from there did not put a foot wrong on a day where mistakes were easy to make. McLaren picked the right moments to pit him, and in the end Norris was just too strong and won by a comfortable margin.

Piastri finished down in sixth, as he struggled to match his team mate for pace. He did have some battles but could not keep the recovering Verstappen at bay, although he did get the better of Lawson.

Lando Norris, 1st

"This was certainly up there with one of our best-ever performances in terms of operational execution, strategy, and pit stop timing. The conditions out there in Brazil were exceptionally tricky, transitioning from Intermediates to slicks on a damp track and back again. We had a difficult launch off the line with wheelspin and lost ground early on, but I stayed patient knowing the weather and potential Safety Cars would bring opportunities back to us. Through flawless communication from the pit wall and keeping the car completely error-free on slicks in the wet, we managed to close down an eight-second deficit, apply pressure on the leaders, and capitalise to take the win.

"The new front wing and upgrade package we introduced this weekend performed exactly as expected, and without them, we would have been further off the frontrunners' pace. However, we have to stay realistic, we were still a tenth or two adrift in outright performance during practice, and we know we are not yet at the level required to contend for a World Championship consistently. I am immensely proud of the entire team and everyone trackside and back at the factory for their relentless work, and we are fully aware that we still have a lot of work ahead of us to extract the ultimate performance from this car.

"Finally, congratulations to Mercedes on their Constructors' Championship, it's a very special achievement and they've done a fantastic job this year in both Championships. I hope they celebrate well and enjoy this moment. We'll be working hard to give them a bit more of a challenge next year."

Oscar Piastri, 6th

"A good result in the end today after a challenging weekend with tricky conditions, especially at the beginning when the conditions were slippery and it took me a while to get into a rhythm. Once I did, the pace was strong, particularly on the Soft tyres, and that’s a real positive. I’m pleased with how competitive we were at points, although sixth feels a little lower than the performance deserved.

"The car felt like it took a step forward this weekend, but we still need to make it quicker and easier to drive and close the gap to Red Bull and Mercedes. Congratulations to Mercedes for their Constructors’ Championship win, I'm looking forward to battling them at the front next season. Now our focus turns to the final three races, we’ll return to the factory to keep working hard and try to carry this progress into the remaining races of the season."

Andrea Stella, Team Principal

"It’s fantastic to be back on the highest step of the podium! This success is truly the result of a team effort. Lando drove exceptionally well in very difficult conditions, proving to be the fastest on both slick tyres and the Intermediates; he didn’t make even the slightest mistake, apart from the incident on the podium!

"Oscar was also very quick: perhaps he spent too long in traffic, but his pace on the dry tyres was encouraging. We should be proud of the work done by the whole team. The upgrades, the car set-up, the strategy, the instructions from the pit wall, and a series of excellent pit stops all contributed to the result.

"The upgrades we’ve brought here are giving us positive signs for the end of the season and have also helped us understand certain concepts ahead of next year. At the same time, we must keep this victory in the right perspective. The low temperatures worked in our favour, whilst Mercedes appeared stronger in higher temperatures. Red Bull, Mercedes and Ferrari will continue to be fierce rivals, so we know there’s still a lot of work to be done.

"Congratulations to Mercedes on the Constructors’ Championship and also to our partners at HPP, who have secured the world title for their power unit for the third year running.

"Finally, I would like to take this opportunity to pay tribute to a great Formula 1 driver, Alan Jones, who passed away a few days ago."

Red Bull

Verstappen’s recovery was never in doubt, such is his record here. The only question was would it be a podium, or the win for the Dutchman. On the inters he was unstoppable, climbing all the way up to fifth from P21 on the grid, but on the softs he lost some pace – while Hadjar had climbed past Antonelli and was running second. Eventually the Dutchman caught his team mate and Red Bull swapped them, but from there Verstappen could not close down Norris for the win.

A double podium was a strong result for the team, with Hadjar having a good scrap with Antonelli before the rain fell a second time. The Frenchman seemed happier in the car at least, after a tricky last couple of races.

Max Verstappen, 2nd

“Starting P21 and making our way up to P2 was a crazy result! We had a lot of fun in the first stint, with great pace and quite a few overtakes, so I was really happy with that. When we switched to slicks, we struggled with a lot of oversteer, which made the car difficult to drive, so I felt there was potentially more in it. Once we switched back to the intermediates, things improved again.

"To finish second here is fantastic. Hopefully next year we can start a bit further up the grid, but racing in the wet always gives you more opportunities, and that certainly helped us today. We scored some important points for the Team in the Constructors’ Championship, so we need to keep pushing, learn from this weekend and carry that momentum into the remaining races”.

Isack Hadjar, 3rd

“It was such a demanding race, with incredibly challenging conditions, but I really enjoyed it. I’ve never faced so many challenges in a single race, but we handled them really well as a Team and I’m very happy we came away with a double podium. A big thank you to the pit crew, who did an amazing job today and helped us stay in the fight.

"I struggled a little during the middle of the stint on intermediates, but things started to improve and we were very competitive on the softs, even with the rain returning towards the end. I really enjoyed the battle with Kimi in the final laps. It was great racing him and even better to finish on the podium alongside two fantastic drivers.

"It’s a really rewarding result for the whole Team. We’re moving in the right direction with the car, and this gives us a lot of confidence heading into the remaining races".

Laurent Mekies, Team Principal

“What a fantastic result for the whole Team here in São Paulo. Max delivered another masterclass drive, fighting his way from P21 to P2 in a way only him can do. That’s now three consecutive podiums here in Brazil from P17 or lower. You could almost say we’re getting used to it, but it never stops being outstanding to watch the way he races here, particularly in such challenging conditions.

"It’s also been a fantastic weekend for Isack. He continued to build his confidence and performance throughout the weekend and delivered a fantastic race today, securing his third podium of the season in an example of clever racing. To have both drivers on the podium is a tremendous reward and true team effort from the whole group. The conditions were incredibly difficult to judge, and the drivers and team executed to perfection, from strategy to pit-stops.

"It wasn’t all straightforward, though. We were very competitive on the intermediates, but from when we switched Max to the dry tyres, we experienced a significant change in balance that made things more difficult. We will need to understand that and keep pushing, because Lando ultimately had a little more pace than us today. Overall, this double podium is a fantastic achievement and a reflection of the hard work, commitment and determination that define this Team.”

Mercedes

Antonelli stormed into the lead off the line and started to disappear up the road, and with Russell making up places from his P7 start, it looked like being a strong race for Mercedes. But it all unravelled midway through, after both pitted for softs. Russell spun in the pit lane exit, losing a huge chunk of time that dropped him back to 10th. Antonelli was complaining about an issue with his car, spinning off at Turn 1 to lose the lead and running wide to lose P2 as well. He continued to drop back and was running a distant fourth when the late rain came.

Russell pitted for inters first and his were up to temperature before Antonelli’s so the team swapped the duo, but Russell then experienced similar issues with his car to his team mate, and thus could not chase up to Hadjar in third. Nonetheless, fourth and fifth was more than enough to seal a ninth Teams’ Championship for Mercedes.

Antonelli was handed a five-second time penalty post-race for an unsafe release in the pit lane, but fortunately for the Italian that did not change his finishing slot.

Kimi Antonelli, 5th

"I'm disappointed with my race today because I really felt the win was there. We had a very strong start and the pace on the Intermediates was really good. Once we switched to the Soft tyre, I was getting into a good rhythm, but I started to feel something strange with the rear of the car. It was very unstable, particularly in some of the high-speed corners, and I then had the spin. That flat-spotted the tyres and compromised the rest of the race. When we put a new set on later, the pace was strong again, so it's frustrating and we need to understand exactly what happened.

"We can put that disappointment aside though because today is a great day for the team. Everyone deserves this Constructors' Championship. It's not only the boys and girls here at the track, but everyone back at Brackley and Brixworth, the support of Mercedes-Benz, PETRONAS and all our partners. They have worked incredibly hard to give us this car and the opportunity to fight for both championships. They helped me achieve my dream last weekend and I'm incredibly happy that today we could achieve this together. I'm very grateful to be part of this team. We'll enjoy this moment, but we want to keep winning, so we'll keep pushing and try to finish the season on a high."

George Russell, 4th

"It was a pretty eventful race today. We had really strong pace at times, particularly on the Soft tyre, and that was a big positive for me. I made a mistake at the pit exit when I was perhaps taking too much risk; I saw an opportunity to fight for the win and wanted to go for it. Ultimately, I don't think it changed our finishing position too much. We struggled more on the Intermediate towards the end, so there are definitely things for us to understand, but overall, I'm leaving this weekend encouraged by my performance. I've been working hard to get back to that level consistently and I've felt much more like myself here.

"Most importantly, we achieved what we came here to do and won the Constructors' Championship. We would have liked to have done it in a bit more style today, but it's an incredible achievement for everyone in the team. We've had four difficult years and the whole organisation put so much work into getting us back into this position. When I joined Mercedes in 2022, we hoped we'd be fighting for championships regularly, so to have gone through that journey and now get back to the top is something we should all be incredibly proud of.

"Winning the Constructors' World Championship is always the ultimate reflection of a team effort. This sport isn't just about the two drivers who are in the car every weekend; it's about the thousands of decisions made back at the factories and the determination of every person who contributes to the performance of the team."

Toto Wolff, Head of Mercedes-Benz Motorsport

"Winning the world championship is a proud moment for every member of our team. F1 is a people business. The trophies may be handed over at the track, but success starts in our factories, in our meeting rooms, on the simulator, in the machine shops, and with every individual who contributes to our performance.

"What makes me happiest today is seeing the reward for that effort. The men and women in Brackley and Brixworth have shown once again what can be achieved when talented people work together with humility, determination and a shared purpose. They have fought for every point, every improvement and every opportunity throughout the season.

"This achievement has also been made possible by the strength of the partnerships that surround our team. PETRONAS has stood alongside us for more than a decade and continues to be an integral part of our performance. Their expertise, innovation and collaborative approach help drive us forward every day, whether through the development of our race fuels and lubricants or their work on advanced sustainable fuel technologies that will help shape the future of motorsport and mobility. We are equally grateful to Mercedes-AMG and the wider Mercedes-Benz organisation for their unwavering support and belief in what we do, and to INEOS for their commitment to our team and our long-term ambitions. Alongside them, our global partner family provides expertise, technology and support that helps us operate at the level required to compete for world championships.

"We will enjoy this achievement because everyone has earned that right. Then, very quickly, our focus will turn to the next challenge. That is the mentality that has shaped this team and will continue to drive us forward. That is more important than ever as today wasn't an easy afternoon for us. We had the pace to win today but suffered during both transition points. We would obviously have liked to finish the job in a more convincing way, but ultimately, we scored the points we needed. These last few races have been challenging at times and today was another difficult one, so there is plenty for us to understand and improve.

"That doesn't take anything away from what this team has achieved across the season though. We started the year incredibly strongly and that gave us the foundation that ultimately got us over the line today. I'm incredibly proud of everyone in this organisation. It has taken us several years to get back to the top, and that has required an enormous amount of determination and hard work from everyone at Brackley and Brixworth. Not many teams have been able to come back from a period like that and win again. This championship belongs to every single person in this team."

Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director

"It was a difficult and eventful race today, and ultimately, we didn't maximise the opportunities we had. Kimi looked in a strong position early on and had good pace on both the Intermediate and Soft tyres, but the spin compromised his afternoon, and we need to understand the unusual balance he reported after switching to slicks. George also showed strong pace at different stages of the race, particularly on the Soft, but also reported similar balance concerns that cost him too. P4 and P5 therefore isn't quite the way we would have wanted to secure the championship, but we did what we needed to do and there were encouraging signs in the underlying performance.

"Winning the Constructors' Championship is the culmination of thousands of hours of work from people right across the organisation. Whilst the results are visible at the racetrack, so much of the performance comes from the effort, expertise and dedication of the teams back in Brackley and Brixworth.

"This season has demanded a huge amount from everyone. We've had to evolve the car, solve problems, respond to our competitors and maximise every opportunity available to us. The way the entire organisation has worked together through those challenges has been hugely impressive.

"As engineers, you're always focused on what can be improved and what comes next, but moments like this are important. Everyone involved in this team should feel an enormous sense of pride in what they have achieved. Winning a Constructors' Championship is one of the hardest things to do in sport, and it is a reward that every member of this team deserves."

Ferrari

Hamilton started from the back and initially made excellent progress, climbing quickly into the top 10 as his team mate struggled and stayed down in P14. But then Hamilton’s rear tyres went off, and he fell back down the order. He was swiftly on the radio calling for slicks, and was the first to swap to the softs. But while that was the right call, later when the rain fell, he was the last to come in for inters and that was the wrong call.

His late stop came after a spin in the slippery conditions, and he did well to recover to the top 10. Leclerc had climbed up the order via a one-stop strategy, and after stopping for inters on the right lap was able to jump his team mate. He had a late fight with Lawson, banging wheels as he passed the Kiwi racer to take P7. But he was handed a post-race time penalty for the incident, which dropped him back to eighth.

Lewis Hamilton, 9th

"We had a strong start and the team did a great job but overall it wasn’t the race I’d hoped for. The first stint was challenging, as we struggled with the rear and found it difficult to get the tyres into the right temperature window. We tried to recover from there and towards the end I felt I could keep pushing but, unfortunately, the rain intensified and I lost some ground as a result. We’ll keep working as a team and do everything we can to deliver a strong result in the next few races."

Charles Leclerc, 8th

"Our execution was good today, we just didn’t have the pace in these conditions. At the start, it was not possible for me to get the tyres to the right temperature and I had no grip on the first stint. Later on, I had the pace, but little free air. At the end of the race, having been patient and made the right choice by staying out on just one set of Softs before switching to the Intermediate, we finished in seventh to bring a few points home, but that’s not our target. There’s a lot for us to learn from this weekend, and we will give it our all for the final three races of the season."

Fred Vasseur, Team Principal

"First of all, congratulations to Mercedes on winning the Constructors’ Championship. They have done a very strong job this season and deserve this success. As for our race we knew it would be a tricky one due to the starting positions and the cold conditions. Lewis had a fantastic start and made up a lot of places, but as the stint progressed his performance dropped off, as was also the case for Charles. Overall, throughout the race we struggled to get the tyres into the right window, which made the car difficult to drive and resulted in inconsistent pace for both drivers. We were lacking performance and we need to understand how we can improve in conditions like these, especially as the next race in Las Vegas could also present us with very low temperatures."

Racing Bulls

Lawson had a great getaway and overtook Norris for P2, running there on merit in the early stages. But once the top teams got their tyres working and started to recover, he gradually fell back down the order. He found himself seventh in the closing stages, and did everything he could to keep Leclerc behind. Those two went wheel-to-wheel and even made contact, with the stewards having a look post-race. They opted to penalise the Ferrari man, which lifted Lawson back to seventh place.

As for Lindblad, He did well to fight back to the top 10 via some highly entertaining battles with the likes of Gasly, Hulkenberg and Alonso. He looked on for an unlikely point from his P18 starting slot, but could not keep the Audi at bay once the rain fell.

Liam Lawson, 7th

"Today was a really good day for us. We had a strong race and made the most of everything we had available. I had great grip on the opening lap and was able to fight with the top teams, but over a long stint we don’t quite have the pace to match them, so I focused on not losing too much time. We’ve had a really decent tripleheader with plenty of positives to take away, and I’ve genuinely enjoyed it. I’ll take a few days to relax and recharge before the final few races of the season. I’m already looking forward to heading back to Las Vegas."

Arvid Lindblad, 11th

"It was an enjoyable race and I had a lot of fun out there coming through from the back. It's disappointing to not come away with any points, especially after showing good pace and genuinely feeling we were in contention for a points finish for most of the race. Unfortunately, things became more difficult over the final 20 laps. I lost quite a bit of time battling Franco and struggled with drivability issues in the wet conditions towards the end of the race. This made it particularly hard to fight Nico as I was trying to keep the car on track. We'll review everything with the team to understand what we could've done better. It's not the way I wanted to end this triple header, as I feel I've made some positive steps forward in terms of driving, but things haven't always gone our way. We'll take the learnings from this weekend, shift our focus and look ahead to the next race in Las Vegas."

Alan Permane, Team Principal

"It's been another strong weekend from the team. It was an exciting first lap from Liam, jumping from third to second and keeping that position for some time. That being said, we have to be realistic that it would've always been a big ask to beat any of the top teams. As such, our focus was on making the correct strategy decisions when it mattered, which we did, meaning Liam finished in P8. Arvid also had a very strong race from the back of the grid to P11. His race pace was very strong, so there are lots of positives to take forward. It's great to be rounding off this challenging triple header with more points as we fight for P5 in the Constructors' Championship. We look forward to a break next weekend before we head to Las Vegas."

Audi

Bortoleto did not have a home race to remember, although at least this year he saw the chequered flag. Starting towards the back after fitting some new engine components, he just did not make any progress in the opening stages and thus was never really a factor out there. Hulkenberg started fourth, but did not get off the line well and immediately dropped places. He picked up a 10-second time penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage when fighting Colapinto, which looked set to leave him without points. But the late rain was a boon to the German, who goes so well in those conditions and found plenty of grip on the inters to overtake Lindblad and score one vital point.

Nico Hulkenberg, 10th

“It's good to come away from such a tricky race with a point. It was an eventful one, as it always is here in São Paulo. There were plenty of curveballs and opportunities for mistakes, but we managed to navigate them well and it was ultimately a fun race. I made a nice move on Lindblad right at the end, managed to set him up on the entry to get a better exit, and used the undercut to gain the position, which felt great, especially after the penalty had put us behind him. To fight back and recover that position, is a satisfying result. Looking at our pace, that's probably the maximum we could achieve today."

Gabriel Bortoleto, 16th

“Obviously, starting from the back didn't make things easy for me, especially in the wet, where overtaking was challenging with the power limitations. I spent quite a bit of time stuck behind other cars, but whenever I had some free air, our pace was quite positive, as it had been all weekend long - it is a shame we could not get more out of it. While my home race was not quite what I had hoped for, the support from the fans was incredible throughout the weekend, and I really appreciate it. Now, a week to recharge and we move on to the next one, still in the fight.”

Allan McNish, Racing Director

“It was a tough race for everybody, with conditions clearly not easy, particularly at the start on the intermediate tyres. Then came the question of when to switch to slicks, before another rain shower towards the end brought the track back towards intermediate conditions.

“From our perspective, Nico fought very well in the wet. We lacked a little bit of pace in the dry, but when the rain returned towards the end, he was able to fight back and reclaim P10, despite having to serve a ten-second penalty for overtaking Colapinto off the track after being pushed wide. The decision is the decision, and ultimately we came away with another point on the board.

“I have to say Nico drove a very strong race, and it was a real demonstration of the fighting spirit across the whole team. We also had a fantastic pit stop, which got him back out close enough to Lindblad to fight for that final points position. That work behind the scenes can sometimes go unnoticed, but it was crucial in giving Nico the opportunity to fight, and he made the most of it.

“For Gabi, starting from the back was always going to be extremely difficult, but he fought his way through to P16. We now reset, regroup and look ahead to Las Vegas in two weeks’ time.”

Aston Martin

Stroll was the only car to retire from the race in Sao Paulo, with the team saying a battery issue prevented the Canadian from continuing. Alonso had a strong race though, a tasty battle with Albon the highlight. After their scrap in Austin, this time around they mostly gave each other space, with Alonso coming through when the Williams man skated wide. But with so few retirements, Alonso wound up just short of scoring at Interlagos and had to carry some damage too, after tagging Bearman at one point.

Fernando Alonso, 12th

“The car felt strong today, particularly in the corners, and we were having some good fights out on track. I think it was one of our most competitive races, but we were struggling for performance on the straights. We made a strong start in the wet conditions, but then I couldn’t avoid contact with Ollie [Bearman] who lost some control of his car in Turn 3. There are positives to take from this weekend, and we need to keep working hard to close the gap for next year.”

Lance Stroll, DNF

“We had to retire the car on Lap 38 due to a battery issue. It’s been another challenging weekend at the end of a long triple header, but we know the areas we need to work on for next year. We now focus on the final push of the season and will use the time before we head to Las Vegas to see where we can make improvements on our current performance.”

Mike Krack, Chief Trackside Officer

“Mixed fortunes for us today: a strong drive from Fernando to finish P12 and Lance unfortunately retiring with a battery issue. Overall we must be satisfied with the outcome of the weekend as we were ahead of competitors with faster cars in Qualifying and Race. We always look forward to racing here in São Paulo – an iconic track with a passionate crowd - so it was great to deliver a strong performance in front of the Brazilian fans.”

Alpine

Thanks to all the grid penalties, Alpine inherited better starting slots than they expected with their double Q1 exit yesterday. Colapinto was 13th and Gasly 15th, and from there the duo got stuck in, fighting their rivals all race long. Colapinto slid off at one point which didn’t help his chances, while Gasly was an interested spectator when Alonso and Albon were fighting. But in the end, the car remained too far off the pace on the intermediates for to fight for points.

Pierre Gasly, 14th

“It was a challenging afternoon for us and it's disappointing not to score points again, especially considering the unpredictable conditions, which I usually really like. We have a lot to review especially with our performance in the wet this weekend as the grip was very poor on both the Intermediates and the Extreme Wets. After yesterday's frustration in Qualifying, we saw some odd things in the aerodynamic data with the car in the wet which I know we are going to take time to review and further understand. I was pretty happy on the Softs in the race today and we were amongst some of the fastest cars on track during the dry part of the race. It's a pity that the last few weeks have not gone to plan but I am looking forward to returning home, having a few days to reset, before fully focusing on Las Vegas where we have been quick in the past.”

Franco Colapinto, 13th

“It has been a tricky race for us, especially with the weather conditions making things very challenging at the wheel. We started on Intermediate tyres and then it was about judging the crossover point to Soft tyres and that was not a straightforward call as the grip levels were quite low. I kept focusing to manage the race and the tyres but then, after struggling for performance, we had to pit again for Softs. The rain shortly came after that and we were back onto Intermediates. Our pace on the Intermediates was not great and that impacted us today and I know the team is looking into why we struggled so much both on Saturday and Sunday in the wet conditions. Still, it was a busy race, we had some good fights on track, which were fun. We will debrief as a team before heading to Las Vegas where hopefully the conditions will suit us better and we can be better placed to compete for points.”

Flavio Briatore, Executive Advisor

“A disappointing end to a weekend where we have, in general, underperformed. It is clear we have work to do to understand how to maximise the car in the wet as it was a weakness for us this weekend. We were amongst the quickest on the Soft tyres in the phase of the race when everyone switched to dry tyres but that soon was no longer the case when the rain returned. There is lots for us to review as a team before we look ahead to the next race in Las Vegas. Finally congratulations to Toto [Wolff] and Mercedes on winning the Constructors' Championship after an impressive and dominant season.”

Williams

It was not to be for Albon, despite a strong Qualifying. He managed to hold onto his top 10 slot for a fair few laps, but then as the track dried, his lack of pace in the Williams was exposed. Nonetheless, the Thai driver had plenty of fun tussles with cars he doesn’t always get to fight with. Sainz made the right call early on, coming in first for the softs along with Hamilton. But that did not help him make up ground and in the end, he finished down the order.

Carlos Sainz, 19th

“Today was a difficult day. The first stint was tough on the inters and I experienced a lot of understeer and graining with the front tyres. By the time I switched to slicks, we had much better pace and were more competitive, but I gambled on staying out hoping for a Safety Car, so by that point it was too late to make a real difference, although the last stint on inters was much better than the first one.

"Tough weekend overall but we now have a week off to reset and recharge batteries ahead of Vegas, where we could potentially be closer to the field. Thanks to everyone for all the effort during this long triple header. We’ll keep pushing until the end of the season.”

Alex Albon, 15th

“We were hoping for more today, but unfortunately we needed the rain to be a bit more steady during the race to maximise our result. We had a good start, and I had some good battles throughout, with a lot of defending, but it was fun racing while it lasted. Ultimately, we didn’t have the pace to fight for points today, and I don't think there was anything we could have done differently. The team made the right calls and we executed a good race in tricky conditions. We'll debrief as a team and see what we can do to come back stronger in Las Vegas."

James Vowles, Team Principal

“Well done to the team; this weekend, qualifying and the race have been some of the trickiest conditions I can remember. Every time, the call from inters to dry to inters, we were on the right tyre at exactly the right lap with Alex. That’s no mean feat at a track where the conditions are changing by the second.

"Well done to Alex, he did a brilliant job from the start and delivered the best performance possible from the car today, but as you can see, it exposed where the car is and where it needs to be. With Carlos, we were a little bit offset and not quite where we needed to be, and we didn’t get the most out of it. But well done to both for persisting in difficult conditions.

"Congratulations to Mercedes on the Constructors’ Championship. Well earned, well deserved, and impressive from start to finish. An aspiration for all of us."

Haas

Bearman started in the top 10 and was running there in the first stint. He dropped back towards the lower reaches of the top 10 as others recovered, but still looking in the mix for points until the pit stop period, when he wound up way down the order after a very slow stop. Camara made it to the flag on debut, in what were more tricky conditions for the rookie to master. He slid off more than once though, but at least brought the car home mostly in one piece.

Oliver Bearman, 17th

“I had a bit of a moment at the start, but nothing major. I lost a few spots but I gained them back again, so it was net zero. After that, I had some very slow pit stops and couldn’t fight back from there. I want to go home now and reset. It’s been a disappointing three weeks where we’ve missed two opportunities to score points – we just need to move on and do better.”

Rafael Camara, 20th

“It definitely wasn’t an easy one, with all the conditions out there we experienced over the course of one race. In the beginning, it was about staying on track, and there were a couple of mistakes – it was a bit tricky. The positive is that there was no damage today and lots learned, but there’s still a lot more to learn for the future. I think there are a lot of things to go through with the team and put in place for next time. On one side, I was trying to enjoy my first race in Formula 1, at home, so it was nice – but I think on my side, I wasn’t fully satisfied with how we finished today. It was a weekend where I think I must’ve nearly experienced everything, so I’ve learned a lot for the future.”

Ayao Komatsu, Team Principal

“It was a pretty tricky race. Ollie had a snap at Turn 3 on lap one, which meant his rear impact structure was a bit damaged, but we didn’t know that at the time – so it had a huge impact on the pit stop. It’s a shame because Ollie’s pace on the first stint – even though we were struggling a little bit to start off with – he came back strong, and was fighting for P10. That really long pit stop, with the car damage, really killed his race. On his last inters stint, we weren’t competitive, so there’s lots to look into.

"For Rafa’s first race in Formula 1, he obviously had very challenging conditions. He had very good pace, and he kept it clean. He made some mistakes, but overall, I think they were very challenging conditions to make your debut, so well done to him for completing this race without any big issues. We know he has performance, he has speed, it’s just about consistency and delivering it. There’s lots of learning today, but we’ve done as best as we could, and we’ll take that forward from here and use it in Las Vegas.”

Cadillac

Bottas failed to start the race after a stuck wheel nut was detected on his wheel on the grid. The team attacked it with a hammer, but to no avail as they wheeled his car back to the garage. Perez did take the start, and managed to beat both Sainz and Camara which was an encouraging result. He was attempting to make the one-stop strategy work until the late rain disrupted that plan.

Sergio Perez, 18th

“I think it was a very difficult race, with mixed conditions between wet and dry. It was very close, so I think we managed to put together a good finish, fighting with the other cars.

“I made a good start and managed to pass him (Bortoleto) straight away. I was then fighting with him and Carlos, but unfortunately, we had a very slow pit stop. I think it’s the same issue we experienced in Mexico, so it’s definitely something we need to work on. We need to make sure we fix our tools and get everything right, so hopefully we can have a much stronger end to the season.”

Valtteri Bottas, DNS

“It’s sad that we were unable to start the race today. Before the lap to the grid, we tried to change the tyre but couldn’t get the right rear wheel nut off. We’re not sure what caused it but we will learn from it and hopefully not face a similar issue again. At least yesterday we were able to demonstrate some decent pace at times. We’ll regroup ahead of the final races and focus on ending the season on a positive note.”

Marcin Budkowski, Team Principal

“It was a challenging day, starting with a cross-threaded wheel nut on Valtteri’s car on the laps to the grid, which unfortunately forced us to retire the car before the start. It is a frustrating end to a triple-header and I want to thank Valtteri and the garage crew for their relentless efforts. We’ll investigate the issue to ensure we don’t suffer a repeat.

“On Checo’s side, he drove well, managing the changeable conditions, and the team made good strategy calls to beat a few of our competitors and finish P18 despite a slow pit stop. The rain ultimately wasn’t disruptive enough to shake up the field, but it was a solid performance from Checo, maintaining pace with our nearest competitors. After a short break, we head back to the US next for our final home race of the season in Las Vegas, which will be a special weekend for the team.”

Pirelli

Dario Marrafuschi, Pirelli Motorsport Director

"Variable weather conditions had a decisive impact on race strategy. Rain before the start left the track with markedly different levels of grip around the lap, making the Intermediate tyre the only viable choice for the opening stint. In these transitional conditions, as the circuit moved from wet to dry, the Intermediate delivered consistent performance and, as the track continued to evolve, tyre lap times progressively closed in on the crossover point for the slicks. We observed predominantly thermal degradation, accompanied by episodes of graining caused by the drying surface, particularly on the right-hand side of the car.

"Once conditions allowed the switch to dry-weather tyres, the Soft confirmed itself as the preferred choice for every team. The relatively low air and track temperatures helped keep degradation under control, to the extent that wear became the main factor to manage in many cases. Some teams were evaluating the possibility of reaching the finish without making any further stops, but the return of rain in the closing stages once again reshuffled the strategic picture.

"Overall, both the Intermediate and the Soft performed in line with expectations, offering teams several strategic options in a race defined by uncertainty over the conditions.

"Congratulations to Mercedes on securing the ninth Constructors’ Championship in its history. It is an achievement that reflects the team’s technical excellence and the quality of work carried out throughout the season, further enhanced by the Drivers’ World Championship title secured by Kimi Antonelli last weekend."

title: Wolff already thinking about 2027 despite constructors' win
excerpt:
Team boss Toto Wolff says he is already thinking about the 2027 season, despite his Mercedes squad clinching their ninth Constructors' Championship in Brazil.

George Russell and Kimi Antonelli finished fourth and fifth in Sao Paulo, securing enough points for the Silver Arrows to claim their first title since 2021, though Wolff said it is not in his character to celebrate.

The result sees Mercedes draw level with Williams on nine championships, with only Ferrari and Mclaren having won more teams' titles – 16 and 10, respectively.

The whole trackside team celebrated on the podium to mark the occasion but, speaking afterwards to F1 TV, Wolff says his mind is on why they didn’t do better in the race itself.

“I'm not celebrating!" he explained. "No, I'm fully on it already. I mean, my team says to me that I'm miserable because I never get to celebrate these moments.

"When the race was finished, Bradley [Lord – Deputy Team Principal] said to me, 'You've got to put at least a smile on your face for the cameras' and I said, 'I can't, you know, this is me!'

"I'm just thinking 'what went wrong in this race? Why have we underperformed? And what can we do for Las Vegas and next year?' But that's just part of my character.”

With nine Constructors' titles won by the Brackley-based outfit, Wolff is now tied with Frank Williams – something the Austrian never thought was possible.

"I had a close relationship with Frank, and to be there, it's amazing," he said. "I can't believe it.

"There's some of our people that have won more than nine, that have been with Brawn, that have been winning with Honda, and they have more. So, yeah, I take it. It's great."

Wolff praised the whole team, both trackside and at the factories in Brackley and Brixworth, for all their hard work in returning Mercedes to the top.

"When I think about the people in our team, what we have in common is an absolute determination to find every inch of performance in every area," he said. "It could be in finance, it could be in aerodynamics. Everybody is constantly driving forward.

"At the same time, we maintain our values. We want to do things the right way, we want to do it with humility, integrity and respect.

"That's something you see when you look at great sporting teams from the past, they were able to achieve success while maintaining that kind of team culture. And that's why I'm proud of everyone in the team."

title: Leclerc and Hamilton lament ‘horrendous’ Sao Paulo GP
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton suffered a race to forget in Sao Paulo as grid penalties, demanding track conditions and tyre struggles combined to produce Ferrari’s lowest-scoring weekend since the Italian Grand Prix.

The Monegasque had faced a 10-place drop for the race start after changing his Internal Combustion Engine (ICE), and a painful opening stint meant that he made minimal progress towards the points.

However, he gradually gained positions through the pit stops and switched to intermediate tyres at the right time, allowing him to cling on as the rain started to fall and eventually fight his way past Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson for P7 on the road. However, he was subsequently penalised for minor contact with the Kiwi and was hit with a post-race five-second penalty, dropping him to P8.

“The execution was okay but the pace was, on the first stint, horrendous for me,” Leclerc said after the race. “Particularly at the start, we just have so many struggles in putting those tyres into temperature.

“It’s unbelievable, and it’s just undriveable. Lewis definitely found a way because he had an incredible start, but for me it was just like driving on ice. Later on I had the pace, but I had very little free air and we also lost a lot of time on the straights, so the first stint was very poor.

“The second stint on the soft was actually pretty good, but not much free air. At the end, by being patient and making the right choice late on, we ended up P7 behind the top three teams. It is the way it is.

“There is so much to be learned. I felt like we were going into the rain and it was like a coin flip – maybe we end up on the right side of things or we end up… it’s just a complete disaster to drive. We’ve got a lot of work to do on that side.”

Contrastingly, Hamilton’s opening laps had hinted at a much stronger day for Ferrari – his grid penalty left him to line up a distant 20th, but he gained 11 positions and seemed to be an early threat to the frontrunners.

However, the performance of his rear tyres rapidly declined and he dropped back down the order, hindered further by an investigation into him leaving the track and gaining an advantage.

To avoid a penalty, he gave the position back to Haas’ Ollie Bearman and went on to establish himself as one of the first to call for a move to slick tyres, which Ferrari agreed with after some back-and-forth over the radio.

The gamble paid off to begin with, but Hamilton only made it to the tail end of the top 10 before he recovered from a spin and found himself stuck in P9, crossing the line a lap behind race winner Lando Norris.

He explained: “I had a great start, and I thought I was on for something positive, then the tyres dropped off almost immediately as the track dried. It’s really hard to then stay on the track. Just massive challenges with getting the tyres in the window and having them working.

“The triple triple [header] has been really tough and challenging for the team, but they’ve done a really amazing job through it all.

"We didn’t get the points I think the team deserved today. I definitely take some of that on me today, with that [spin] at the end. We live and we learn and we move on.”

title: Leclerc and Antonelli hit with post-race penalties in Brazil
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli have been handed five-second time penalties for separate incidents at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, with the former held responsible for causing a collision with Liam Lawson over the final laps while Mercedes released Antonelli in an unsafe manner.

Looking to recover as many positions as possible following what he labelled a "horrendous" opening stint at Interlagos, Leclerc steadily closed the gap down to the Racing Bulls driver amid increasing rainfall.

As their tight battle for seventh developed, the Monegasque tapped the left rear wheel of Lawson's car at Turn 12 before sweeping around the outside to demote the New Zealander on the penultimate lap.

The stewards determined that the contact merited a time penalty for Leclerc, and with Lawson crossing the line just under two seconds behind, the pair have subsequently swapped places in the race classification to leave Leclerc eighth.

"The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 16 (Charles Leclerc), the driver of Car 30 (Liam Lawson), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video and in-car video evidence and determined that Car 16 made contact with Car 30 at turn 12," the verdict read.

"While the contact was minor and Car 30 was able to maintain the lead thereafter, thedriver of Car 30 claimed that the contact damaged the rear left rim of his car and also enabled Car 16 to get closer to him on track and then eventually overtake him 5 corners later. Furthermore, under the Driving Standard Guidelines, Car 30 had the right to the corner and it was for Car 16 to take the necessary steps to avoid a collision.

"The driver of Car 16 claimed that it was a minor contact with no obvious sporting consequence. While we acknowledge that the contact was minor, having examined the fight on track between the two cars, we conclude that Car 16 was able to get closer to and thereafter overtake Car 30 because of the contact. The contact clearly disrupted Car 30 and allowed Car 16 to pull up alongside when it was further away before the contact. This was an obvious sporting consequence.

"In mitigation, the wet conditions coupled with the nature of the contact (ie minor) was taken into account in imposing a 5 second time penalty as opposed to a 10 second time penalty."

Antonelli was also penalised for an unsafe release after Mercedes inadvertently sent him into the path of Alpine’s Franco Colapinto in the pit lane, forcing the Italian to swerve in order to prevent contact.

Although five seconds has been added to his race time, he retains P5 thanks to what was originally a 20-second advantage over sixth-placed Oscar Piastri.

The official document explained: “The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 12 (Kimi Antonelli), team representative and reviewed video and in-car video evidence and determined that Car 12 was released in an unsafe manner when Car 43 was approaching in the fast lane.

“While Car 12 was entitled to travel down the pit lane in parallel to cars in the fast lane, in this instance, Car 12 momentarily lost control on the slippery surface and had to take steps to avoid a collision and that resulted in a potentially unsafe situation.

“The team acknowledged that this release could have been handled better and in a safer manner.”

In a similar incident, Haas driver Ollie Bearman has been handed a five-second time penalty after he was released in an unsafe manner just as Leclerc was passing him in the pit lane.

However, he had enough of a lead over Cadillac's Sergio Perez to hold onto P17, which marked a missed opportunity for points after he started from a career-best sixth on the grid.

"The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 87 (Oliver Bearman), the driver of Car 16 (Charles Leclerc), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, and in-car video evidence," read the stewards' document.

"BEA was released from its pit stop into the path of LEC, which was already proceeding along the pit lane. As a result, LEC was forced to brake and take evasive action, being squeezed towards the pit wall on the right-hand side.

"The Stewards determined that BEA was released in an unsafe manner and therefore imposed a 5 second time penalty."

title: 'No idea what happened on that pit exit' spin – Russell
excerpt:
George Russell admits he has "no idea what happened on that pit exit" after suffering a spin in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, but has hailed Mercedes' performance this year after the team secured the Constructors' Championship.

Russell just missed out on pole for Sunday's 71-lap race at the Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace, but started P7 due to a five-place grid penalty for an Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) change.

Having moved up to fourth during a wet opening, Russell spun on the exit of the pit lane after switching to slick tyres, eventually recovering undamaged but having lost several positions.

The Briton charged up the order and was the first to switch back to intermediate tyres as rain fell again in the closing stages, eventually finishing fourth after being allowed ahead by Mercedes team mate, Kimi Antonelli.

The result means Mercedes have claimed the teams' title for the first time since 2021, with Russell having joined the team in 2022.

"An incredible achievement from everyone in the team. We had four tough years, and to come through and take the championship is really, really great," said Russell.

"Obviously, it was a bit of an up-and-down race. I have no idea what happened on that pit exit. I probably just took too much risk, because I was seeing an opportunity to go for the win at that point, but it happened.

"Ironically, because that happened, I then didn’t pit for another set of slick tyres, and it kind of put me back in the same position as I was before the incident. The most important [thing] is we got the championship sealed."

Russell sits third in the drivers' standings, 17 points behind Max Verstappen after the Red Bull driver surged from P21 to second during the Grand Prix.

Despite missing out on the rostrum, Russell was pleased with the general performance of the Mercedes and admitted finding pace was his priority ahead of another title tilt in 2027.

"It’s been a very positive weekend in terms of my performance. I’m probably more happy coming away from the weekend, because the performance was good," he said.

"At this stage, I care more about the performance than I care about the result, because that’s what’s been my weak point.

"The performance yesterday was great, the performance on the soft tyre was really great today, but obviously I did make that mistake. It probably would have been a very different picture if we’d have started P2, but yeah…"

title: Verstappen reflects on 'challenging' P21 to podium charge
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has highlighted how key his first stint was in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix as the Dutchman stormed to the podium from the back of the grid, navigating "weird balance" issues along the way.

The four-time World Champion started P21 on the grid for Sunday's 71-lap race at the Autódromo José Carlos Pace, having had several power unit component changes made on his car that confined him to a back-of-the-grid start.

Over the opening laps on a wet but drying track, Verstappen quickly climbed into the points and was on the fringes of the podium when drivers began to pit for slick tyres.

Through the middle phase of the race Verstappen moved up to second, eventually finishing 14 seconds adrift of race winner and polesitter, Lando Norris, after a late pit stop for intermediate tyres with rain falling again.

"Yeah, it was a challenging race," said Verstappen. "I think the first few laps, of course, were very important.

"I overtook a lot of cars, and actually, that first stint, I think on the intermediates, was really, really strong.

"Unfortunately, after that, I don't know if we picked up some kind of damage because the car felt like the complete opposite to anything that I've felt the whole weekend, with some really weird balance.

"Unfortunately, once I got into P2, I couldn't really make any inroads. So we have to understand what went wrong there. But, I mean, starting P21 and being on the podium in second, I think, is a very good result."

The Interlagos circuit has proved to be a happy hunting ground for Verstappen in recent years, winning the Grand Prix in 2024 from P17 on the grid during a wet affair, while he converted a pit lane start into P3 just 12 months ago.

It proved to be an especially good day for Red Bull, with Isack Hadjar securing a double podium for the team, it's second of the season after the duo achieved the feat in Baku.

Having started P5, the Frenchman climbed up to P2 during the middle part of the race but was told to give the position up for Verstappen after running wide and losing time at Turn 1.

"It was so, so difficult, so challenging, especially switching from the intermediate to the soft tyre, avoiding the traps," said Hadjar.

"It was extremely difficult, especially in the pit lane. You saw how tricky it was to drive, and then more rain at the end.

"So happy to be standing third today. But I need to keep making a bit less mistakes because I could have avoided a little awkward situation with Max.

"So yeah, just want to apologise because I think on that stint I could have kept it a bit more on the track."

Hadjar also had to withstand pressure from Antonelli as rain fell in the closing stages and before drivers pitted for intermediate tyres, with the Red Bull driver admitting he nearly crashed in the pits.

"I was testing the grip for him [Antonelli], basically," said Hadjar. "I could see he was challenging me a lot, and I was on ice, and he was on ice as well, but it was well managed.

"I nearly shunted into my pit crew when boxing, but they did a fantastic job. They kept their calm, and the pit stop was fast. So big thanks to the boys."

title: Norris delighted to ‘give back’ to McLaren in Sao Paulo win
excerpt:
Lando Norris was thrilled to be able to give McLaren “a little bit of reward for their hard work” by winning the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, which marked his and the team’s third victory of the season.

Although the Briton started from pole position on the damp track, he quickly lost places to Kimi Antonelli and Liam Lawson, but recovered well to move up to second place and set his sights on the race lead.

As the surface dried out, Norris was amongst the first to switch from intermediate to slick tyres, giving him a clear advantage in terms of grip when he returned to challenge the Italian for first place.

A spin for Antonelli opened the door for him to sail back through, and he maintained the position amid more rain and another round of pit stops to cross the line over 14s ahead of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen.

“It was a very tough race – very, very tough,” Norris reflected. “Obviously, not the best of launches off the line, but a lot of challenges today, obviously, with the conditions.

“Going onto slicks in the wet is always tough, especially when you're pushing for the lead and trying to catch up a little bit.

“The main thing today was I just kept it cool and I didn't make any mistakes. I had the pace when I needed to, so it was good. Nice to be back on the top step, and what a place to do it as well.”

McLaren had slightly dropped away from the likes of Mercedes, Ferrari and Red Bull in recent rounds, but upgrades introduced at Interlagos seemed to provide the boost required to get back in the mix.

While Norris had looked strong throughout Free Practice, his skills in the wet made the difference in both Qualifying and the Grand Prix, leaving him grateful he was able to maximise every opportunity over the weekend.

Norris said: “We're trying, you know. I'm trying my best, and I think this weekend we had an opportunity to get pole yesterday, we had an opportunity to win.

“I feel like most times this year, when there's been an opportunity, I went for it and we've been able to achieve it. So I have to say a big thanks to the team because they're still working very hard.

“It's annoying when you can't give them a good result back, like the last few weeks. But certainly this weekend, I feel like we've been able to give something back to them and give them a little bit of reward for their hard work. So always a big thanks to them, and we have to keep pushing till the end of the year.”

title: Lewis Hamilton frustrated after costly spin: 'I didn't get that information'
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has detailed that he didn't get information about track conditions prior to his high-speed spin in Sao Paulo.

In the closing stages of the race, rainfall began to hit the circuit, creating a headache for the teams and the drivers.

However, it quickly became apparent that a switch back to the intermediate compound would be needed after slicks were used in the mid-part of the race following a wet start.

Hamilton was one of the last drivers to make the stop for intermediates and did so after suffering a spin on the climb up the hill after Turn 12.

Although he was able to avoid terminal damage, it cost Hamilton valuable time.

"It was so gutting, honestly," Hamilton told media including RacingNews365.

"In those greasy conditions, I was quicker than Lawson. I was catching him by a second a lap, and they said [on] the previous lap, 'It's going to stay consistent like this'.

"I was like, 'okay, I can stay out in this'. Just before the pit entry, they said 'box, box' and I was just behind Lawson, so I just pressed overtake.

"I thought the conditions were staying the same. So I was like, 'okay, I'm not going to stop this now, I'm good'.

"I get to Turn 1, and it's drenched, so I didn't get that information. We were unfortunate with that."

[Article continues below]

Hamilton 'lucky' to avoid wall contact

Hamilton went on to end the race in ninth place, while team-mate Charles Leclerc crossed the line in seventh.

The result was Hamilton's worst finish of the year, bar his retirement at the Spanish Grand Prix.

However, the seven-time champion knows he was lucky not to add to his retirement tally.

"I was just trailing around trying to bring the car back, I was lucky I wasn't in the wall," he said.

"Sorry to the team on that, but overall I think the team did a really great job this weekend. We didn't have the pace we wanted."

title: Max Verstappen seeking Red Bull investigation after 'extreme' Sao Paulo swing
excerpt:
Max Verstappen is eager for Red Bull to understand how his RB22 car suffered an "extreme" swing in balance in the Sao Paulo GP.

From 21st on the grid after a power unit change, in the early wet conditions, Verstappen sliced through the field, with Lewis Hamilton from 20th - with the Dutchman up to sixth place by Lap 8 after passing Alex Albon, Oscar Piastri, and Nico Hulkenberg.

Through the two stops for slick tyres, and then through the final change back to intermediates, Verstappen climbed to second place behind dominant winner Lando Norris to record a third straight podium at Interlagos after either starting from the back or pit-lane.

His haul of 18 points further cements the Red Bull driver into second place in the drivers' standings, and is now 17 points clear of George Russell and 18 clear of Lewis Hamilton after a seventh podium in the last eight races, and 11th in the 13 races since the Austrian GP.

However, post-race, Verstappen described how his car suddenly had "extreme amounts of oversteer" after the cross to slick tyres - and was unsure of the cause.

"The first laps were fun and hectic, but you had to be patient as well; it was very slippery out there," Verstappen told Sky Sports F1.

"Of course you are finding grip in other places, but it is very easy to make a mistake, so you can look like a hero, but you can also very quickly go to zero, so I think we did well.

"I very quickly moved myself to the front, but then something went wrong with the car when we went from inters to the softs.

"I had extreme amounts of oversteer in the high-speed corners, so that means you try to rebalance that, but it kills your front tyre.

"So we need to understand, and I don't want to say [something] failed, but what actually went missing or broke on the car because I do think there was much more in it, but unfortunately, for most of the race, the car was just not working well.

"Because when we switched back to the intermediates at the end, the car was completely the opposite balance of what I had in the beginning - and that is normally not possible."

Verstappen then indicated that the issue was not part of the car degradation he has reported in previous races, and that "something probably fell off or broke."
