title: Liam Lawson earns extra points as Charles Leclerc hit with post-race penalty
excerpt:
Liam Lawson has been promoted to seventh place in the final Sao Paulo Grand Prix results after Charles Leclerc was handed a post-race time penalty.

On lap 69 of 71 in the wet conditions, Leclerc biffed Lawson out of the way at Turn 12 to get a better run up the hill - and eventually got past for the position on the next lap at Turn 4 to take seventh on the road, with Lawson eighth.

Lawson doubted Leclerc's move was legal post-race, and felt it was his "speciality" after a similar move on Alex Albon in the 2017 GP2 race in Abu Dhabi.

Lawson finished 1.816s behind Leclerc on the road, but the incident was take to the stewards, where a five-second time penalty was applied for the Monegasque, meaning the two swapped places, with Lawson now seventh and Leclerc in eighth.

It means Lawson earns an extra two points to his tally, taking him to 89 for the season, and Leclerc drops from 251 to 249.

In their investigation, and after speaking to both drivers, the stewards found that Leclerc's action "clearly disrupted" Lawson - and so handed a five-second sanction instead of the usual 10-second one for causing a collision.

"The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 16 (Charles Leclerc), the driver of Car 30 (Liam Lawson), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video and in-car video evidence and determined that Car 16 made contact with Car 30 at turn 12," began the report.

"While the contact was minor and Car 30 was able to maintain the lead thereafter, the driver of Car 30 claimed that the contact damaged the rear left rim of his car and also enabled Car 16 to get closer to him on track and then eventually overtake him 5 corners later.

"Furthermore, under the Driving Standard Guidelines, Car 30 had the right to the corner and it was for Car 16 to take the necessary steps to avoid a collision.

"The driver of Car 16 claimed that it was a minor contact with no obvious sporting consequence.

"While we acknowledge that the contact was minor, having examined the fight on track between the two cars, we conclude that Car 16 was able to get closer to and thereafter overtake Car 30 because of the contact.

"The contact clearly disrupted Car 30 and allowed Car 16 to pull up alongside when it was further away before the contact. This was an obvious sporting consequence.

"In mitigation, the wet conditions coupled with the nature of the contact (ie minor) was taken into account in imposing a 5-second time penalty as opposed to a 10-second time penalty."

title: George Russell concedes to 'high-risk' stakes in Sao Paulo F1 pit-lane spin
excerpt:
George Russell has explained what happened during his costly pit-lane exit spin at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

With the field starting on intermediate tyres, the track began to dry over the opening stint, with Lewis Hamilton and Carlos Sainz the first to pull the trigger on Lap 15 for the change to red-marked slick dry soft tyres.

Russell was in the gaggle of cars which stopped next time by from fourth place, with Lando Norris, Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson, and Oscar Piastri also stopping at the same time.

Russell was set to rejoin behind Norris, as he had entered, but on the pit-lane exit, he spun and briefly blocked the track as Hadjar, Lawson, and Piastri filtered past, with Russell losing a further place to Nico Hulkenberg's Audi.

Ultimately, the time lost, around 30s, prompted Russell to switch to an attempted one-stop strategy for dry tyres, not stopping when the rest of the field did when the slicks had worn out.

Then, when the rain returned in the closing stages, Russell was able to save a pit-stop, and came in for the intermediates, as he took fourth place, to help Mercedes seal the constructors' crown.

Reflecting, Russell spoke of the surprising upside of the "high-risk" decision.

"I'm not really too sure what happened," Russell told media, including RacingNews365 of the spin in the pit-lane.

"I went quite high risk because I smelt an opportunity and paid the price.

"It is in those moments you either gain a lot or you lose a lot, and this time, it went against us.

"Ironically, because of that, I didn't pit [for a second time for softs], and it kind of brought me back into the race.

"I showed really strong pace on the soft; we had the fastest race pace, and it has been quite a while since I've had this race pace, so I will take the positives out of that."

[Article continues below]

Russell explains late pit-stop

Explaining further about the late change to intermediates from the slicks, Russell praised his team and pointed to the turnaround after his fury at being told to abort his lap in qualifying that he felt was good enough for pole position.

"It was a huge benefit. The team did a great job there, and I think it just highlights the challenges of this sport, and [in qualifying], we got it wrong," he said.

"[In the race], they got it perfectly, and the other drivers got it wrong, and that is just how it goes, and it is always highlighted more when it goes wrong than when it goes right."

title: Liam Lawson casts doubt over 'legality' of race-defining Charles Leclerc overtake
excerpt:
Liam Lawson has cast doubt over the legality of Charles Leclerc's late overtake on him for seventh place in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

On lap 69 of 71 in the wet conditions, Leclerc biffed Lawson out of the way at Turn 12 to climb the hill, with the right-front tyre making contact with Lawson's left-rear, forcing the New Zealander wide.

This then gave Leclerc better momentum up the hill, and although Lawson stayed ahead into Turn 1, the Ferrari driver got ahead for seventh place on the road into Turn 4 on the next lap after a thrilling wheel-to-wheel battle.

Lawson finished eighth, but could capitalise if Leclerc is handed any penalty, as he was 1.816s behind over the line.

Leclerc has been called to the stewards regarding the incident for allegedly causing a collision, with Lawson saying the move reminded him of Leclerc's move on Alex Albon in the 2017 GP2 race at Abu Dhabi - where Leclerc did a 'bump and run' on Albon into the hairpin before the long back straight, using this momentum to get ahead for the win.

Reflecting, Lawson branded the move as Leclerc's "specialty."

"I think it was his wing which hit my tyre, so I think we got really lucky," Lawson said of Leclerc's move to media, including RacingNews365.

"I feel like it was exactly like his GP2 move on Albon in Abu Dhabi years ago; he did the same kind of thing, so maybe it is his speciality.

"I don't know if it is legal or not, and we'll go and review it, but it was a good battle overall."

[Article continues below]

Potential Antonelli attack

Fast-starting from third, Lawson initially felt he could have attacked leader Kimi Antonelli and taken the lead of a grand prix for the first time.

"It was a crazy race, honestly, I had a really good start, good grip into Turn 1 and made a place up and was thinking I might try and attack Kimi at some point in the lap," he said.

"But once the pace stabilised, they're a lot quicker than us, and we started to fall back, we were damaging the tyre quite a lot more than them, and then the pace in the dry was okay.

"At the end, I tried to keep Charles before, we had some contact into Turn 12 , ended up losing the place."

title: Lewis Hamilton reveals 'ballooned' moment that played havoc in Sao Paulo
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has revealed that the rear tyres on his first stint in his Ferrari "ballooned and overheated" during a chaotic São Paulo Grand Prix

From the 20th on the Interlagos grid following a multitude of power unit penalties, Hamilton started brilliantly, rising to ninth by the end of the first lap.

But from there, his race slowly unravelled, initially on the opening set of intermediates in the wet conditions before making a superb early call to switch to the soft slicks.

Running on a second set of soft Pirellis late in the race, Hamilton spun up the hill as he was preparing to return to the pits for a new set of inters, kissing a barrier with the rear wing of his SF-26 as he tried to control the slide.

The seven-time F1 champion ultimately finished ninth and a lap down on race winner Lando Norris in his McLaren.

Speaking to Sky Sports F1 after the race, Hamilton explained how the handling problems hit almost immediately once the lights went out.

"A really tough day and weekend for the whole team, but they've done a really great job, switching out the engine, making sure the car was as strong as it could be," said Hamilton.

"We struggled in the dry, but I had a great start. Unfortunately, the rear tyres just ballooned and overheated, and I then struggled.

"After that, I was pushing to go to the slicks, which I eventually got on. I was one of the earlier ones, and was feeling pretty good. It was very tricky in those conditions.

"And then we ended up having an extra stop, and I had a lot of ground to cover from there.

"At the end, the last message I got was that it was going to stay drizzling, and I was like, 'Okay, this is my moment to keep pushing', and I could stay in those conditions.

"I didn't hear that it was raining more in the first sector, and I passed the pit lane, got to Turn 1 and it was wet, so that unfortunately lost us a couple of places, otherwise, the team did a great job."

With three rounds remaining in the season, Hamilton admitted he was unsure what to expect from Ferrari's pace heading into the final stretch.

"I really don't know where we're going to be in the next races, but we've had a really good car in the past races," he said. "This weekend was a bit of a struggle.

"I think that the team deserved a better result. But we live and we learn, and we will come back and try and fight harder at the next one."

title: Toto Wolff responds to matching F1 icon feat: 'Never thought it possible'
excerpt:
Toto Wolff has conceded that he "never thought it possible" he would match the feat of F1 icon Sir Frank Williams.

For the ninth time, Mercedes are constructors' champions, overseen by team principal Wolff, who has now drawn level with Williams for third on the all-time list.

The title was confirmed after a messy race in Brazil, where Lando Norris took victory for McLaren ahead of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar, with George Russell and Kimi Antonelli salvaging fourth and fifth for Mercedes despite a difficult afternoon.

Russell had started seventh after a five-place grid penalty, whilst he also spun in the pit lane exit at one stage after a wet-to-dry tyre change.

Antonelli also spun twice, once before the start and again at Turn 1 while running at the front, as he struggled to get temperature into his tyres.

It was Mercedes' first race of the season without a podium finish, but it did not matter: the result was enough to put the title beyond Ferrari's reach with three rounds still to run.

Asked about matching Williams's tally, speaking to Sky Sports F1, Wolff said:

"Obviously, Frank is such an unbelievable icon of the sport, and to be tied on constructors' championships, I never thought that was ever possible," he said.

"I had a close relationship with Frank, and to be there, it's amazing. I can't believe it.

"But also, fair justice. There are some of our people who have won more than mine, who were with Brawn, winning it with Honda, God knows what, and they have more. So yeah, I take it. It's great."

Reflecting on the shape of the campaign overall that has yielded the first constructors' title after its run of eight from 2014 to 2021, Wolff added: "It's amazing.

"It was a very strong beginning of the season, and that got us over the line. These last few races, there have been some challenging times.

"Today, it was difficult, but overall, I'm so proud of the organisation.

"We've taken a few years to be back in the top spot. Not many teams have been able to come back from such a situation, and it just shows the great work, the great people that we have in our organisation, and it's fantastic to be among them."

excerpt:
Lando Norris suffered another podium disaster in his smashing celebrations at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Norris claimed his third victory of the season in Interlagos in a wet and wild race, beating Max Verstappen by 14.6s and Isack Hadjar by 24.4 to record his 14th career victory, and first since the Netherlands in August.

However, after the British national anthem and receiving his trophy, Norris went to conduct his usual podium celebration of smashing the champagne bottle to spray it - but unfortunately, he did so too hard and smashed the bottle to the ground.

He then took a few moments to compose himself after the smash - which is the second podium incident he's had.

After the 2023 Hungarian GP, when he smashed the champagne bottle, he accidentally did so too close to Verstappen's winner's trophy, knocking it off the top step and smashing it.

title: Max Verstappen bemoans 'completely opposite' feeling despite Sao Paulo stunner
excerpt:
Max Verstappen described a "completely different" and "weird" feeling with his Red Bull during another superlative performance in the São Paulo Grand Prix.

For the third consecutive year, Verstappen started from a position that suggested a podium was highly improbable, yet for the third consecutive season, the four-time F1 champion managed to finish in the top three, claiming the runner-up spot on this occasion after starting 21st

Two years ago, Verstappen won from 17th on the grid; last season, he was third from the pit lane.

Assessing his latest heroics in a wet-dry-wet race, the Red Bull driver, speaking to Sky Sports F1, said: "It was a challenging race.

"I think the first few laps, of course, were very important. I overtook a lot of cars, and actually, that first stint, I think, on the inter was really, really strong."

Verstappen made most of his headway on the first set of inters before a switch so softs prevented further major progress.

"Unfortunately, after that, I don't know if we picked up some kind of damage because the car felt completely opposite to anything that I felt the whole weekend, with some really weird balance," he said.

"Unfortunately, once I got into P2, I couldn't really make any inroads. So we have to understand what went wrong there."

After another inter spell late in the race as the rain fell again, Verstappen finished 14 seconds behind race winner Lando Norris.

He at least acknowledged his performance, however, adding: "I mean, starting P 21 and being on the podium in second is a very good result."
